title: Poke
description: One still frame of a tree against a summer sky, from a clip filmed on a tripod in the wind. Twenty-six seconds of its real motion were taken apart into the tree's own vibration modes: twelve shapes, each with the frequency and damping the clip measured, from a slow 0.36 Hz sway of the whole crown to quicker 1.3 Hz shivers in single branches. The crown is not shown as a photograph but engraved: lines cut along the contours of the leaves' light on a cobalt-shadow ground, each one swelling where the leaves are lit. Take hold of any part of the tree and pull. The whole crown answers through the modes it shares with that spot, each part with its own lag, and the lines bend with it and draw out along the way they move. Their colour turns with where each part is in its swing: gold with your hand, violet against it, teal as it leads, rose as it lags, or either as it swings aside, deeper the harder it moves. Let go and everything rings down in its own time, coupled the way the real branches are. Nothing about the motion is invented.
intent: Image-Space Modal Bases / Interactive Dynamic Video: Abe Davis, Justin G. Chen and Fredo Durand, 'Image-Space Modal Bases for Plausible Manipulation of Objects in Video', ACM Transactions on Graphics 34(6), SIGGRAPH Asia 2015 (https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/137568, https://www.provideocoalition.com/pokemon-go-interactive-dynamic-video/), the method that Generative Image Dynamics (Li, Tucker, Snavely and Holynski, CVPR 2024) drives with a diffusion prior. Here it runs on real footage, as in the original. Offline (tools/depth/bakes/poke): DIS optical flow from a reference frame to all 772 frames, photometrically checked; Frequency Domain Decomposition (Brincker, Zhang and Andersen 2000) of all the motion at once, so every singular vector at a spectral peak is a complex 2D mode shape; the twelve strongest spatially coherent ones kept; frequency and damping from an SDOF fit to each modal coordinate's spectrum; quantised into a 12-layer texture array. Live: complex modal oscillators driven by the hand, a closed-loop spring over a hand-sized patch of the crown (the Gaussian-weighted mean shape, so incoherent shivers inside it cancel) whose force is projected onto the modes (f_i = phi_i(m)^H F). The unit-norm shapes leave relative modal mass free, so they are tilted by (f0/f)^2 toward the slow crown-wide modes, which makes a pull swing the whole crown rather than one clump. The tree is matted over a filled, regraded sky and cut into jittered Voronoi patches, each translated rigidly by the mean modal field around it, so leaves move instead of stretching; a seam no patch claims falls back to the continuous backward warp. Inside the matte the photograph is not drawn: the crown is rendered only as a line engraving on a cobalt-shadow ground. Its lines are evenly spaced streamlines (Jobard and Lefer 1997) of the contour direction of the leaves' luminance (the smoothed structure tensor of its gradient), seeded in shuffled jittered order and outward from each finished line, cut into strokes of varied length; each stroke is an instanced ribbon whose width at every spine point is the leaves' light there. Every spine point is carried by the modal field at its own rest position, so a pull bends the strokes where the crown shears, and each stroke is drawn out along its displacement (its trailing end lags by a share of it, eased into a cap). The tint is the angle of the analytic signal sum_i phi_i (q_i - i v_i / omega_i) in the frame of the pull, on a continuous OKLCH hue wheel (gold with the hand, violet against it, teal leading, rose lagging, either one swinging aside), its chroma rising with the amplitude, so a frozen still shows the twelve-mode structure as gradients across the crown. Developed through the lab film kit (summer). Patent note: MIT holds a patent on this method (Davis et al., image-space modal bases / interactive dynamic video). This is a non-commercial portfolio reimplementation of the published paper; clear it before any commercial use. Stills: ?poke=x,y,amp[,deg]&t=seconds (print uv, pull as a fraction of the print's width toward deg, default left; t after letting go, omit to hold), ?still=1 stops the breeze.

sources.author: Engin Akyurt (https://www.pexels.com/@enginakyurt/)
sources.note: 1920x1080, 29.97 fps, 25.8 s, locked off on a tripod. Reference frame 382 (the frame closest to the clip's mean pose). Flow with OpenCV DIS at 960x540, modal grid 320x180. Tree matted off the sky by colour and a guided filter; sky behind filled by push-pull and regraded toward the genre's cobalt (polariser-like, deeper at the top).
